card.name: Adverb before a participle like administered
card.fires_on: An adverb ending in -ly (orally, concomitantly, commercially) that sits right before a past participle such as administered, used, marketed or inhaled. It also fires on the ending of 'concomitantly' in 'concomitantly used'.

modes.label: orally before a participle
modes.description: The word 'orally' right after 'of' and before administered or inhaled.
modes.example: the absorption of<< orally>> administered griseofulvin, thus

modes.label: concomitantly used
modes.description: The ending of 'concomitantly' before 'used' in drug-interaction warnings about enzyme inhibitors or inducers.
modes.example: In addition, discontinuation of a concomit<<antly>> used cytochrome P450

modes.label: commercially marketed
modes.description: 'commercially' before 'marketed' in a description of a formulation.
modes.example: containing povidone (not the<< commercially>> marketed formulation) or a vehicle nasal spray

card.writes: It prepares a participle that modifies the noun, much like the Chinese promoted tokens meaning 'used', 'issued' or 'produced' (的 relative-clause endings).
card.plain: It marks an adverb like 'orally' or 'concomitantly' that is about to be followed by a verb form like 'administered' or 'used'.
